metadata.title: Why CLAUDE.md Breaks When It Gets Too Long
metadata.purpose: vox-explainer slate cut. Mechanism: CLAUDE.md's instructions compete with other context for Claude's attention; beyond ~200 lines the probabilistic instruction-following degrades and key rules are ignored; the fix is to keep CLAUDE.md lean by offloading workflow content to Skills and enforcing inviolable rules as Hooks.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro am_onyx, VOICE-LOCK) — actual_duration_s below is measured from mp3s
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL = short CLAUDE.md / rule followed; CRIMSON = long CLAUDE.md / rule ignored; never swap mid-film
metadata.note: Exclusions honored: NO context-window math or token-count discussion, NO comparison with other tools' context files, NO full Skills/Hooks explanation. One mechanism: CLAUDE.md length degrades compliance; stay under 200 lines, offload to Skills/Hooks.

props.segment: Why CLAUDE.md Breaks When It Gets Too Long
props.command: Why does CLAUDE.md stop working past two hundred lines?

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. The teacher's CLAUDE.md has a clear rule on line twelve: Vanilla CSS only — no Tailwind. The project is on its third build. Claude generates a component. It uses Tailwind classes. The rule is still there on line twelve.

items.label: Third build
items.sub: Claude generates a component using Tailwind classes.

items.label: Rule ignored
items.sub: The rule is still there on line twelve — Claude does not follow it.

card.copy: Why CLAUDE.md breaks when it gets too long

beats.narration_text: Session one: forty-seven lines. Stack rules. Code style. Environment quirks. Never-rules. Claude follows the Vanilla-CSS rule every time. Session two: eighty lines. Grading workflow notes. New never-rules. Lessons-learned entries. Still working. Session three: the simulation build. Sprint goals added. Architecture notes. A colleague's phone number. Four near-duplicate CSS rules. Two-hundred-twenty lines.

production_viz.label: CLAUDE.md grows: 47 → 80 → 220 lines across three builds
production_viz.mechanic: three vertical bars growing taller in sequence — 47 lines (teal), 80 lines (teal), 220 lines (crimson at the top portion); labeled with the line counts

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] growing document bar with compliance meter

beats.narration_text: Here is the question. Adding more rules to CLAUDE.md should make Claude more reliable. Here is the project where Claude began ignoring key rules as CLAUDE.md grew past two hundred lines. Why?

items.label: Add rules
items.sub: More instructions should make Claude more reliable.

items.label: Past 200 lines
items.sub: Claude begins ignoring key rules as CLAUDE.md grows.

items.label: Why?
items.sub: The rule is still on line twelve. Adherence dropped anyway.

beats.narration_text: CLAUDE.md is advisory. Claude reads it at session start. It tries to follow it. The compliance is probabilistic — Claude may sometimes generate code that violates a CLAUDE.md rule, especially under prompt pressure. In a short file, the Vanilla CSS rule is prominent. In a three-hundred-line file, it competes with sprint goals, duplicate entries, personal reminders, and workflow notes that should be in a Skill.

production_viz.label: signal vs noise — the rule competes for attention
production_viz.mechanic: two bars side by side: short file (teal, tall) where 'the rule' is prominent; long file (crimson, tall) where 'the rule' shares the page with sprint goals, duplicates, personal notes — a signal-to-noise chart

beats.narration_text: The example. After the simulation build, the teacher's CLAUDE.md is at two-hundred-twenty lines. Claude generates Tailwind classes on a new component despite Vanilla CSS only on line twelve. The teacher trims to ninety-five lines. Moves grading workflow to a Skill. Converts the grade-generation rule to a Hook. Claude respects the CSS rule again.
beats.scene_description: a title card with the before/after line counts and a one-line result
beats.image_prompt: B05, editorial title card: '220 lines → 95 lines' with the sub-line 'Rule respected again', EB Garamond, cream ground, ink text, terracotta accent under the arrow

build.needs: SCRIPTING GAP — B05 has no drawable spec. Author a diagram, a Remotion pattern, or a Manim scene. Do not fill this with generated media.

beats.narration_text: The fix has three moves. Keep CLAUDE.md under two hundred lines — the five categories that belong in it: bash commands, code style deviations, test runners, architectural decisions, environment quirks. Move workflow content to Skills — on-demand files that are not loaded at session start. Convert inviolable rules to Hooks — scripts that execute regardless of what Claude decides.

production_viz.label: three moves: trim, Skills, Hooks
production_viz.mechanic: three labeled rows drawing in teal: 'Trim CLAUDE.md — under 200 lines'; 'Move workflows to Skills'; 'Convert rules to Hooks'

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: your CLAUDE.md is long and Claude isn't following some of the rules in it. Ask Claude to explain the length failure mode — what happens to rule adherence as CLAUDE.md grows — and give you the rule for what to cut, what to keep, and how short is short enough.

props.segment: Why CLAUDE.md Breaks When It Gets Too Long

beats.narration_text: The compliance meter. Short CLAUDE.md: rule-following high. Past two hundred lines: compliance begins to degrade. Past three hundred: key rules get ignored under prompt pressure. The meter is not about line count for its own sake — it is about signal-to-noise. Every entry added dilutes every other entry.

production_viz.label: compliance meter: high at 50 lines, dips at 200, fails at 300
production_viz.mechanic: a horizontal axis showing line count (50, 100, 200, 300); a compliance curve starting high (teal), staying flat to 150, beginning to dip at 200, falling at 300 (crimson); labeled milestones

beats.narration_text: The practical move: audit your CLAUDE.md now. For each entry: does Claude know this from the code already? Cut. Does this change session to session? Move it to TODO.md. Is it a workflow? Move it to a Skill. Must it hold every time without exception? Convert it to a Hook. What remains is what belongs.

production_viz.label: four audit questions for each CLAUDE.md entry
production_viz.mechanic: a four-row decision table drawing in: 'Claude infers it from code → cut'; 'Changes session to session → TODO.md'; 'A workflow → Skill'; 'Must hold always → Hook'

beats.narration_text: A maintained fifty-line CLAUDE.md beats an abandoned five-hundred-line one every time. The rule on line twelve works when it is the most specific thing on the page. It stops working when it is noise.

items.label: 50 maintained
items.sub: A maintained fifty-line CLAUDE.md beats an abandoned five-hundred-line one.

items.label: Most specific
items.sub: The rule works when it is the most specific thing on the page.

items.label: Or noise
items.sub: It stops working when it is noise.

card.copy: Short and specific. Not long and aspirational.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. CLAUDE.md is advisory, and Claude's compliance with it is probabilistic. Under two hundred lines, rules hold. Past three hundred, key rules get ignored under prompt pressure. The fix is three moves: trim CLAUDE.md, move workflows to Skills, convert inviolable rules to Hooks. Signal-to-noise is what compliance tracks — not line count for its own sake.
